draft.title: Genomes, genes and alleles
card: Genome
all of an organism's DNA, including the genes and the DNA between them.
Gene
a section of DNA that codes for a product, such as a protein. A gene sits at a set position on a chromosome.
Allele
one version of a gene. Different alleles of the same gene can code for slightly different products.
An organism can carry two different alleles of one gene, such as one for attached earlobes and one for free earlobes. This is one reason individuals of a species differ.
draft.remember: The genome is all the DNA. A gene is one section of it, and alleles are versions of that gene.

a.q: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between a gene and its alleles?
opts: Alleles are different versions of the same gene
Alleles are different genes found in the same genome
Alleles are the products that a gene is copied from
Alleles are sections of DNA that sit outside any gene
a.why: An allele is one version of a gene, so alleles of a gene occupy the same position and code for variations of the same product. They are not separate genes, because separate genes code for different products.
a.clue: Think of alleles as versions of one thing.

b.q: Priya's dog has one allele for black fur and one allele for brown fur at the same gene. Which statement about this dog is correct?
opts: Both alleles are versions of one gene in its genome
The two alleles are two different genes in its genome
The brown allele is not part of the dog's genome
The dog's genome is only the gene for fur colour
b.why: Black and brown are two versions of a single fur colour gene, and both are DNA in the dog's genome. Calling them two genes is tempting, but different alleles of the same gene are versions, not separate genes.
b.clue: Is the genome bigger or smaller than one gene?

a.best: Alleles are different versions of the same gene

b.best: Both alleles are versions of one gene in its genome

problems.detail: Earlobe attachment is used as an example of two alleles of one gene. This is an outdated myth: earlobe attachment is polygenic, with dozens of loci identified, and it varies continuously. Use a genuine single-gene example, such as the dog fur colour gene in question b.

The clue 'Think of alleles as versions of one thing' echoes the right option's wording ('different versions of the same gene'), so a student could match the word 'versions' without understanding the idea.

check.summary: The card uses attached and free earlobes as a single-gene, two-allele example, which is a scientific myth (the trait is polygenic) and should be replaced. Question a's clue also gives away the answer by repeating the word 'versions'.
